author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Matthew Jodouin shares how, despite a stable and supportive upbringing, he became lost as a teenager and turned to drugs, alcohol, and self-destructive choices. His life shifted only when a mentor stepped in - someone outside his family who believed in him before he could believe in himself. Through this transformation, Matthew highlights how mentorship provides connection, perspective, and hope, especially for young men who often struggle in silence with anxiety, depression, and addiction. Blending personal recovery with research and reflection, he argues that mentorship is not a luxury but a necessity. By creating spaces for connection and showing up for others, we can help young men rediscover purpose and change lives, including our own.

title: Why young men need mentors now more than ever | Matthew Jodouin | TEDxSurrey

description: We live in a split screen society. Nationally, we agree that we need to build more housing, more transmission lines, more transportation infrastructure. But, when we learn about developments proposed for our own neighborhood, our first reaction is often negative. This TED talk unpacks the reason for this disconnect and offers architectural epidemiology as a solution. When we use data to guide design conversations with the community, we can speed the permitting process by turning a new development from a cause for community concern into a cause for celebration. Adele Houghton, FAIA, DrPH, LEED AP, is President of Biositu, LLC where she works at the intersection of buildings, public health, and climate change. She is a member of the American Institute of Architects College of Fellows and received a Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) degree from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, where she also teaches. Her book Architectural Epidemiology (Johns Hopkins University Press, 2025), c
title: Building Faster and Fairer | Adele Houghton | TEDxUWMadison

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Burial of the dead is one of the clearest archaeological signs of the depth of human emotional and social ties. Investigation of some of the oldest burial evidence hints at the ways these ties connect us with other species much older than our own.  John Hawks is a world expert on human evolution and genetics. He is Chair of the Department of Anthropology and Vilas-Borghesi Distinguished Achievement Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He also serves as a visiting professor at the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa.  

Hawks’ research covers seven million years of human origins. His work in human genetics helped uncover the very rapid recent pace of genetic evolution with the rise of agriculture. He was one of the first to show how genes from ancient groups like the Neanderthals could make a difference in today’s people. For the last decade, he has worked with scientists and explorers in South Africa to bring to light new hominin fossils. Among the best known
title: The meaning of ancient burials | John Hawks | TEDxUWMadison

For over a century, we've measured students against a standard built for a world that no longer exists. This talk makes the case for replacing one-size-fits-all standardized tests with personalized assessments that measure the skills actually required to thrive in the age of AI. Justin "Mr. Fascinate" Shaifer is an award-winning STEM thought leader, educator, and keynote speaker on a mission to empower the world with innovation.

At Fascinate Media, he serves as both executive producer and on-camera talent, creating educational content about innovation, AI & STEM literacy, and the Future of Work. His roster of past clients and collaborators include LinkedIn, Intuit, NVIDIA, Google, PBS, Discovery, Bill Nye the Science Guy, and Al Roker. description:
How can we transform the way we inspire a love of reading in a generation raised on screens, algorithms, and constant distraction? The answer lies in re-embracing something deceptively simple: children’s literature. These stories, often dismissed as small or simplistic, carry astonishing power and identity. They help people imagine new possibilities, see themselves reflected with imagination, and step into identities and experiences different from their own. In moments of cultural division and rising book bans, children’s literature becomes even more essential. It is both refuge and revolution: a safe place to explore who we are, and a bold space to ask who we can become.
 
At Bowling Green State University, we see every day how stories shape future teachers, families, and entire communities. When educators lean into the narratives that shaped them, and invite students to do the same, they model courageous teaching: teaching that welcomes curiosity, celebrates identity, and nurtures b
title: Why Children’s Books and a Love of Reading Matter  | Karen Wilhelm & Nicole Skilliter | TEDxBGSU

author: TEDx Talks
description: When words are not enough, somatic art therapy gives the body and imagination a language to heal trauma. Dr. Lexi Morgan is a Board-Certified Art Therapist (ATR-BC) and Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) with nearly a decade of clinical experience supporting individuals and groups in healing from trauma. She brings over 30 years of personal experience using art as a survival tool and a pathway to healing, which inspired her professional journey into the field. Her doctoral research explores the integration of somatic art therapy with body-based practices, showing statistically significant and lasting effects in reducing burnout and PTSD after just one day of intervention. Lexi's work highlights the accessibility and power of creativity, imagination, and the body in releasing what is stuck and no longer serves us. In her practice and research, she emphasizes how the combination of creativity, curiosity, compassion, and community can transform how we live our day to day lives
title: Art Gives the Body a Voice | Dr. Lexi Morgan | TEDxCharleston

description:
In a world dominated by screens, our eyes silently bear the burden of our digital lifestyles. Yet, they keep sending us signals—dryness, strain, headaches, blurred vision, and fatigue—that often go unnoticed.
In this TEDxWCESangli talk, Dr. Nidhi Patwardhan, renowned ophthalmologist and founder of Nandadeep Eye Hospital, uncovers the hidden impact of excessive screen time on eye health. Through scientific research, real-life observations, and powerful visual evidence, she reveals how reduced blinking, meibomian gland dysfunction, and rising myopia are becoming modern epidemics.
This talk is a wake-up call to decode the unsent messages from our eyes before temporary discomfort turns into lasting damage. Discover practical habits, preventive measures, and the surprising “magic drug” that can help protect your vision in the digital age.
 Dr. Nidhi Patwardhan is a respected ophthalmologist, eye health educator, and the driving force behind Nandadeep Eye Hospital. With years of clinical ex

description: In order to address youth violence at its core, systems must begin to break silos and start viewing “high-risk” juveniles as the wounded children they are, with limitless potential, in search of a village to belong to. With a bachelor’s in marketing and a master’s in educational transformation from Georgetown University, Jerome’s career has centered around reimagining how communities empower youth. He has founded storytelling ventures, educator networks, and now leads Charleston’s first wraparound, focused deterrence model for high-risk youth. His philosophy is simple: "Everything in our society was once a figment of someone's imagination. Therefore, any aspect of it can be reimagined..." description: A look at how C. elegans, a millimeter-long worm living in soil and compost, helps scientists study complex nervous systems. Using one gene (UNK-1) as a case study, this talk shows how researchers can see proteins, switch them off on command, and link tiny biological changes to visible behavior—showing why this tiny worm has played such a big role in modern biology. I am a 10th grade student from San Francisco, California. I have a passion for science and specifically biology. Over the past 3 years I have pursued this interest by working on genetics and neuroscience at a Lab at Stanford University. Today I will share how studying a tiny animal can reveal big discoveries about our brain. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

From cutting edge meta-materials to the psychology of waste, this talk explores why solving our energy challenges requires more than engineering alone. Because true efficiency begins with how we think. As a future physicist and engineer, I love seeing the logic behind things. Rather than just accepting things as they are, I prefer looking beyond the surface, tinkering and asking questions. I'm Shaunak, a year 12 student, studying Maths, Further Maths, Physics and Chemistry. I love to read, my latest obsession being chaos theory - the explanation behind something as small as a butterfly's wings being able to stir up a hurricane. Outside of the classroom, I play badminton for a club and at tournaments. Although I haven't won any yet, I'll keep trying until I do! title: The Philosophy of Waste | Shaunak Gupta | TEDxDCGS Youth

description:
A shark's skin could hold the key to reducing millions of tonnes of carbon emissions. Discover how biomimicry is transforming transport by applying nature's engineering to modern technology. A fascinating example of how small changes can create global impact. I am a Year 12 student studying Maths, Further Maths, Physics and Chemistry at A Level. I chose these subjects because I enjoy problem-solving and understanding how things work, which has led to a strong interest in engineering.

I am hoping to pursue a career in mechanical or aeronautical engineering, where I can combine creativity with technical thinking to solve real-world problems. I am currently focused on building a strong foundation through my A-level studies.

Outside of studies, I enjoy playing the piano, keeping active and playing football. I am currently captain of the King’s Church U17 football team where I enjoy the competitive spirit, as well as the teamwork and discipline it requires. This talk was given at a TEDx

description:
In a world where AI can translate anything, is learning another language still worth it? This talk explores the surprising neurological and social benefits of bilingualism, from brain health to cultural connection. What do we lose when technology does the thinking for us? Hello, my name is Audrey Kay, a Year 12 student currently studying Biology, Chemistry, Maths and German for my A levels while taking German a year early - an incredibly rewarding experience.

Alongside my academic studies,  I am also a very creative person who enjoys many other hobbies, including producing and writing songs using FL studio and synthesised vocals with the program Utau. I also play bass, violin and piano and I am passionate about digital art, providing me with much needed balance in my stressful week.

I aspire to become a doctor and be able to help create a tangible difference in people’s lives. It's really important that my job would be fulfilling and if I could lighten someone’s load who is struggli
title: The Medical and Social Case for Bilingualism | Audrey Kay | TEDxDCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: What does faith look like in an increasingly secular world? Drawing on the ideas of Charles Taylor and more, this talk explores how religion, belief, and meaning may evolve in the future. A thought provoking look at faith in the modern age. I am currently taking English, Drama, RS and Politics A Levels. My passions are acting, writing, playing video games and reading. In an ideal world I would work in either the creative sphere of film and theatre, or further pursue academia and in turn law. I have played roles such as The Groom in Lorca’s ‘Blood Wedding’, Andrea in Brecht’s ‘The Life of Galileo’, Mrs Wilberforce in ‘The Ladykillers’ and most recently O'Brien in ‘1984’ . My interest in theology originated from religious connotations within literature like the Amber Spyglass, and poetry such as that of Ted Hughes. title: Future of Faith, Religion and Theology: What That Might Look Like | Kit Wolsey Pont | TEDxDCGS Youth

The most powerful technology of the future may be too small to see. Discover how Smart Dust could revolutionise the world while raising profound questions about privacy, security, and control. Outside of the workshop, I like to play piano (to questionable degrees of success) at Grade 8, have entered more game development competitions than I can ever finish projects for, and consider losing a tabletop game to friends a mortifying wound. I can proudly say I’ve attempted sports like badminton and rock climbing; whether any success has been made is a different story entirely.

description: What if schools were designed not just for learning, but for wellbeing? This talk explores how architecture, colour theory, and nature inspired design can transform educational spaces. Rethinking schools from the ground up to help students thrive. I currently study Art, Drama, and Maths A-level. I have always been passionate about the creative arts, and have loved drawing from a young age. In the future, I hope to pursue a career in either architecture of acting. Architecture surrounds us throughout our lives, I am particularly interested in the profound impact buildings have on our psychology. Meanwhile, theatre inspires me to push past my limits, while also getting to know myself in more depth throughout the process. Between revision and an obscene amount of art coursework, I love to read, DJ, and run. description:
The same algorithms that guide drones, rovers, and navigation systems can teach us something about life. Explore the surprising power of optimisation, pathfinding, and goal setting in a rapidly changing world. Because success is not always about working harder. It is about choosing the right path. Hi, I'm Rishi, an aspiring engineer, mathematician, entrepreneur and a proud Arkwright Scholar. Currently in Year 12 at Dr Challoner's Grammar School, I study Maths, Further Maths, Physics, and Electronics.

Outside of academics, I love playing squash and badminton (with more enthusiasm than ability!), I'm interested in cars and technology, and I'll always get stuck into anything building-related. I also love to bake and cook, recently I've been experimenting with making Neapolitan style pizza, with varying degrees of success…

description:
What if your personality is not who you are, but simply a pattern you have learned? This talk challenges the idea that personality is fixed, exploring how beliefs, habits, and perspectives can be reshaped over time. Because changing your future may start with changing yourself. I am a sixth-form student studying History, English Literature, Mathematics and Economics and I am currently completing an EPQ exploring how cognitive bias influences the application of justice in law, an interest that reflects my aspiration to pursue a career in international arbitration or commercial law. 

Alongside my academic work, I am a Grade 8 classical guitarist and also play piano for enjoyment. I enjoy reading, baking, watercolour painting and writing short stories and I have even had the opportunity to fly a two-seater aircraft. I previously competed at county level in both swimming and hockey and I also designed and made my own prom dress at sixteen. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TE
title: What If Your Personality Is Just a Pattern? | Pranshi Gupta | TEDxDCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Could the NHS withstand the next biological crisis? Using COVID-19 as a case study, this talk explores the strengths, vulnerabilities, and future preparedness of healthcare systems in the face of biological threats. A timely look at resilience in an increasingly uncertain world. I am Lochana Suraneni, a Year 12 student at Dr Challoner's Grammar School studying Biology, Chemistry and Maths. For my EPQ, I investigated the extent to which COVID-19 accelerated workforce shortages in the NHS, building insight through interviews with over five consultants and engagement with professors. I hold a diploma in public speaking and am currently pursuing a post-diploma in classical dance. Beyond academics, I have contributed to published books and been featured in local newspapers for charity dance performances at Parliament and Trafalgar Square. My interests include long-distance walking, speed skating, acting competitions, archery, singing and violin. I aspire to study medicine, seeking a career
title: Could the NHS Withstand a 'Bio-War'? | Lochana Suraneni | TEDxDCGS Youth

description: Is Bitcoin a passing trend, or the next evolution of money? This talk examines the strengths and weaknesses of modern currencies and explores whether Bitcoin could redefine how we store and exchange value. The future of finance may depend on the answer. My name is Matthew Tharaniyil George, attending Dr Challoner's Grammar School. I do 4 A -Levels, being Maths, Physics, Economics and Politics. I have a vested interest in how our global economy works and how each person can contribute value while bettering themselves in the process. As someone who believes in maximising efficiency and leaving welfare decisions up to the people they impact, I have explored how an economist reasons and creates solutions to problems in the present day, drawing on skills such as maths, politics and social science in order to find solutions myself. title: The Future of Money | Matthew Tharaniyil Goerge | TEDxDCGS Youth

description:
What if changing your future starts with changing your perspective? This talk explores how the way we view challenges, opportunities, and ourselves can shape the path ahead. A powerful reminder that mindset can be a catalyst for transformation. I am an academically driven aspiring law student with a strong interest in Politics and Human Rights. I am particularly motivated by the role of law in promoting justice, accountability and social change. I am keen to develop a career that combines rigorous legal analysis with meaningful societal impact. 

I take Maths, Politics and History A-Levels as well as an EPQ, researching differences between countries criminal justice systems. I enjoy Acting and Public Speaking as I have previously performed on a West End stage for an awards show. I am also passionate in self defence as a Black Belt in karate. description:
Freedom and justice are not guaranteed. They are defended. From Magna Carta to modern debates over AI, this talk makes the case for preserving trial by jury. A powerful reminder of why ordinary people remain central to democracy. Studying English Literature, History and French has allowed me to explore how ideas, cultures and perspectives intersect, an interest shaped in part by living in both France and Switzerland. 

I am particularly interested in medieval and gothic literature and French cinema, alongside legal history, explored further in my EPQ on how integral justice was to the 1215 Magna Carta. 

As a regular participant in the debating society and founder of Sapientia, DCGS’ student newspaper, it has been excellent building a platform for discussion. 

Outside academia, I write extensively and love playing squash. I hope to study English Literature at university, with ambitions to go into the legal world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: Can Trial By Jury Survive an Age of Efficiency? | Alexander Deakin-Radkov | TEDxDCGS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When we talk about domestic abuse, we tend to reach for language; reports, testimony, legal procedure. But what if the most powerful thing a survivor can offer is not words, but paint?
Red is an artist who began making work not as a career, but as an act of survival. Confined to bed with the physical effects of PTSD following an abusive relationship, she turned to painting, and over eight years created a collection of over thirty works that began as private grief and grew into something far larger than herself.
Informed by neuroscience, which shows that visual images can allow empathy to arise before judgement takes hold, Red makes the case for art as a form of advocacy; a language capable of reaching the legal and political systems that so often fail to see the full reality of survivors' lives.

title: Standing in Their Shoes: How Survival Art Becomes Systemic Change | RED - | TEDxPorthtowan Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Can technology keep up with a world of 8 billion people and counting? From hydroponic farming to desalination, this talk explores the innovations helping humanity meet its growing demand for food and water. But as we depend more on technology, are we also becoming more vulnerable? When choosing my subjects at DCGS, I was drawn to the logic of the sciences. Biology and Chemistry are the essence of life on Earth and Maths is puzzling, challenging and fun and is inextricably linked to technology and innovation, which opens doors to aid humans within our planetary biosphere. 

My interests are numerous, and I love projects. I am curious about how people think and how that shapes society. For example, Darwin's Origin of Species created a social storm that still prevails today in the ideas of religion, science, politics and within the wider society's ideology. description: Can we trust AI if we cannot understand how it thinks? Explore the hidden world inside neural networks and the growing field of AI interpretability. A fascinating look at the future of safe and transparent AI. I'm Aviral, a Year 12 student at Dr Challoner's Grammar School studying Maths, Further Maths, Physics, and Computer Science. I've always been into technology, and recently I've become really interested in data science and AI, and I'm currently aiming for a career in it, and I've been working on a few coding projects on the side to keep building on that. Outside of school I play guitar, go hiking, and play tennis. I'm looking forward to speaking at TEDxDCGS and getting to talk about some of the things I think are going to matter most going forward.
